text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- More than a dozen members of the former 32 Battalion have approached the Truth and Reconciliation Commission, seeking amnesty for their role in pre-election violence in South Africa in 1994.
- Five accident deaths were reported over a black weekend on Namibia's roads.
- Outstanding government debt has soared to N$1.9 billion from N$731 million since independence, according to the latest quarterly bulletin of the Namibian Economic Policy Research Unit.

- The debate about the alleged selective recruitment of soldiers for the Namibian Defence Forces was revived in parliament on Friday, with the opposition saying members of the former South West African Defence Force were discriminated against.
